questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of git aliases?
options: Git aliases provide short names for command sequences or commands, configured in Git settings. They can improve consistency but should remain transparent, documented and safe for teammates to understand.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Git aliases provide short names for command sequences or commands, configured in Git settings. They can improve consistency but should remain transparent, documented and safe for teammates to understand.
questions.explanation: Git aliases provide short names for command sequences or commands, configured in Git settings. They can improve consistency but should remain transparent, documented and safe for teammates to understand.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git config --get-regexp "^alias\."` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with git aliases?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
